rows.output: Otu Labour Party agaghị abụ nke mbụ na-akwado echiche dị otú ahụ, ebe otu Green Party kwere nkwa izu ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n'oge mgbasa ozi ntuli aka ha n'afọ 2017.
rows.reference: Labour Party agaghị abụ ndị izizi kwadoro echiche a, ebe Green Party kwere nkwa ịrụ ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu n’ime oge ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị 2017.

rows.source: The aspiration is currently not being endorsed by the Labour Party as a whole, however.
rows.output: A na-achọghị nkwado nke Labour Party n'ozuzu ya ugbu a.
rows.reference: Labour Party anaghị akwado ebumnuche ahụ ugbu a dịka otu, kosiladị.

rows.source: A Labour Party spokesman said: 'A four-day working week is not party policy and it is not being considered by the party.'
rows.output: Onye na-ekwu okwu otu Labour kwuru: "Otu izu ọrụ nke anọ abụghị iwu otu pati ma a nọghị na-eche echiche."
rows.reference: Onye nkwuchite okwu Labour Party kwuru: ‘Ọrụ ụbọchị anọ n’izu abughị amụma ndị otu a nke na ndị otu a anaghị atule ya.’

rows.source: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell used last week's Labour conference to flesh out his vision for a socialist revolution in the economy.
rows.output: Onye isi oche John McDonnell ji ọgbakọ Labour nke izu gara aga mee ka echiche ya pụta ìhè maka mgbanwe socialist na akụnụba.
rows.reference: Shadow Chancellor John McDonnell jiri ọgbakọ Labour mere izu gara aga were kọwapụta echiche ya maka mgbanwe na akụnụba.

rows.source: Mr McDonnell said he was determined to claw back power from 'faceless directors' and 'profiteers' at utility firms.
rows.output: Ọkammiri McDonnell kwuru na ya na-agbasi mbọ ike iji ike n'aka ndị isi na-enweghị ihu na ndị na-erite uru na ụlọ ọrụ na-enye ọrụ.
rows.reference: Mazị McDonnell kwuru na o kpebiri iweghachite ikike site na n’aka ndị ‘isi ụlọ ọrụ amaghị’ yana “ndị nrite oke uru’ n’ụlọ ọrụ ndị eji ebi ndụ.

rows.source: The shadow chancellor's plans also mean current shareholders in water companies may not get back their entire stake as a Labour government could make 'deductions' on the grounds of perceived wrongdoing.
rows.output: Onye isi oche na-ahụ maka onye na-ahụ maka ego na atụmatụ ya na-eme ka ndị na-etinye ego ugbu a na ụlọ ọrụ mmiri ghara inweta ego ha niile azụ, n'ihi na gọọmentị Labour nwere ike ime 'mwepu' n'ihi mmebi iwu.
rows.reference: Atụmatụ shadow chancellor ahụ pụtakwara na ndị nwere oke n’ụlọ ọrụ mmiri nwere ike ha agaghị enwetacha isi ego ha, maka gọọmentị Labour nwere ike ‘ime mwepu’ na ndabere ebumnobi ihe ezighi ezi.

rows.source: He also confirmed plans to put workers on company boards and create Inclusive Ownership Funds to hand 10 per cent of private-sector firms' equity to employees, who stand to pocket annual dividends of up to £500.
rows.output: Ọ kọwara atụmatụ itinye ndị ọrụ n'ụzọ dị iche iche n'ime ụlọ ọrụ na ịmepụta ego nke gụnyere itinye 10 pasent nke ụlọ ọrụ nkeonwe n'aka ndị ọrụ, bụ ndị ga-enweta ego ruru £500 kwa afọ.
rows.reference: O kwuputakwara atụmatụ itinye ndị ọrụ na bọdụ ụlọ ọrụ ma mepụta Inclusive Ownership Fund ga-enyefe pesenti 10 n’oke ụlọ ọrụ ndị nkịtị n’aka ndị ọrụ, ndị nwere ike inweta uru isi ego ruru £500.

rows.source: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy tell "60 Minutes" whether the FBI's investigation of Kavanaugh could change their minds
rows.output: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy gwara "60 Minutes" ma ọ bụrụ na nyocha FBI nke Kavanaugh nwere ike ịgbanwe echiche ha
rows.reference: Lindsey Graham, John Kennedy gwa “60 minutes” ma nyocha ndị FBI enwere ike ịgbanwe obi ha

rows.source: The FBI investigation into accusations against Judge Brett Kavanaugh has delayed a final vote on his nomination to the Supreme Court by at least a week, and raises the question of whether the bureau's findings could sway any Republican senators into pulling their support.
rows.output: Nyocha FBI banyere ebubo eboro onye ọka ikpe Brett Kavanaugh emeela ka a na-eme ntuli aka ikpeazụ ya dị ka onye ọka ikpe nọ n'Ụlọikpe Kasị Elu ka ọ dịkarịa ala otu izu, ma na-ebute ajụjụ ma ọ bụrụnụ nyocha ahụ nwere ike ime ka ndị Republican ọ bụla na-akwado ya wepụ nkwado ha.
rows.reference: Nyocha ndị FBI na-eme banyere ebubo eboro Ọka Ikpe Brett Kavanaugh egbuola oge ime ntuli aka ikpeazụ na nhọpụta ya maka Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu opekempe otu izu, wee bulite ajụjụ na nchọpụta ụlọ ọrụ ahụ enwere ike ịgbanwe obi ndị ọmebe iwu Repọblikan ịdọrọkwa nkwado ha.

rows.source: In an interview airing Sunday, "60 Minutes" correspondent Scott Pelley asked Republicans Sens. John Kennedy and Lindsey Graham whether the FBI could unearth anything that would lead them to change their minds.
rows.output: N'ime ajụjụ ọnụ na-aga n'ihu na Sọnde, onye nta akụkọ "60 Minutes" bụ Scott Pelley jụrụ ndị Republican Senators John Kennedy na Lindsey Graham ma ọ bụrụ na FBI nwere ike ịchọta ihe ọ bụla ga-eme ka ha gbanwee echiche ha.
rows.reference: N’ajụjụ ga-eme na Sọnde, onye akụkọ “60 Minutes” Scott Pelley jụrụ ndị Ọmebe Iwu Repọblikan John Kennedy na Lindsey Graham ma FBI enwere ike bọlite ihe ọ bụla ga-eme ka ha gbanwee obi ha.

rows.source: Kennedy appeared more open than his colleague from South Carolina.
rows.output: Kennedy pụtaworo ka ọ dịkwuo n'ihu karịa onye òtù ya si South Carolina.
rows.reference: Kennedy meghere onwe ya karịa onye otu ya si South Carolina.

rows.source: "I mean, of course," said Kennedy.
rows.output: "Ọ bụ ihe m na-ekwu, n'ezie," ka Kennedy kwuru.
rows.reference: “Ana m eche, ee,” Kennedy kwuru.

rows.source: "I said going into the hearing, I said, I've talked to Judge Kavanaugh.
rows.output: "Agwara m na ị na-aga n'ihu, agwara m, agwawokwa m onye ọka ikpe Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: “E kwuru m na nbanye na nnụrịta ụka ahụ, E kwuru m, A gwara m Ọka Ikpe Kavanaugh okwu.

rows.source: I called him after this happened, that allegation came out, said, 'Did you do it?'
rows.output: Mụ na ya kọrọ ya mgbe nke a mere, mgbe ebubo ahụ pụtara, wee sị, 'Ị mere ya?'
rows.reference: Akpọrọ m ya ka nke a mechara, ka ebubo ahụ pụtara, kwuo sị, ‘Ị mere ya?

rows.source: He was resolute, determined, unequivocal."
rows.output: Ọ dị njikere, na-eme atụmatụ, na-enweghị mgbagwoju anya."
rows.reference: Ọ kụjaghị, ọ nwere mkpebi, na enweghị mgbagha.”

rows.source: Graham's vote, however, appears set in stone.
rows.output: ntụli aka Graham, n'agbanyeghị, dị ka a ga-asị na ọ dị n'elu nkume.
rows.reference: Ntuli aka Graham, kosiladị, dịka edeela ya ede.

rows.source: "My mind's made up about Brett Kavanaugh and it would take a dynamite accusation," he said.
rows.output: "Obi m adịla mma maka Brett Kavanaugh na ọ ga-ewerekwa ebubo dynamite."
rows.reference: “Obi m ekpebiela gbasara Brett Kavanaugh, na ọ ga-ewe ebubo dasiri ike,” o kwuru.

rows.source: "Dr. Ford, I don't know what happened, but I know this: Brett denied it vigorously," Graham added, referring to Christine Blasey Ford.
rows.output: "Dọkịta Ford, amaghị m ihe mere, mana amaara m nke a: Brett jụrụ ya nke ukwuu," Graham gbakwunyere, na-ezo aka na Christine Blasey Ford.
rows.reference: “Dr. Ford, Amaghị m ihe mere mana a ama m nke a: Brett gọnarịrị nke ukwuu,” Graham gbakwunyere, na-arụta Christine Blasey Ford aka.

rows.source: "And everybody she names couldn't verify it.
rows.output: "Ma onye ọ bụla ọ kpọrọ aha enweghị ike ịkwado ya.
rows.reference: “Na ndị niile ọkpọrọ aha enweghị onye kwetara ya.

rows.source: It's 36 years old.
rows.output: Ọ dị afọ iri atọ na isii.
rows.reference: Ọ gbaala afọ 36.

rows.source: I don't see anything new changing."
rows.output: Achọghị m ịhụ ihe ọhụrụ na-agbanwe."
rows.reference: Anaghị m ahụ ihe ọhụrụ na-agbanwe.”

rows.source: What is the Global Citizen Festival and Has it Done Anything to Decrease Poverty?
rows.output: Kedu ihe Global Citizen Festival bụ na ọ mere ka ịda ogbenye belata?
rows.reference: Gịnị bụ Mmemme Global Citizen, na Ọ nwela Ihe Ọ Bụla Ọ Mere Iji Belata Ụbịam?

rows.source: This Saturday New York will host the Global Citizen Festival, an annual music event which has a hugely impressive line-up of stars performing and an equally impressive mission; ending world poverty.
rows.output: N'ụbọchi Satọdee a, New York ga-anabata mmemme Global Citizen Festival, mmemme egwu afọ nke nwere usoro ndị na-eti egwu na-eme ihe ngosi na ebumnuche dị egwu; ị kwụsị ịda ogbenye n'ụwa.
rows.reference: Satọde nke a New York ga-achịkọba Global Citizen Festival,emume ịgụ egwu a na-eme kwa afọ nke na-enwe ahịrị ndị ama ama na-atụ n’anya nke ukwuu na-eme ihe nkiri, yana ebumnobi dịkwa ịtụnanya; ịkwụsị ụbịam n’ụwa.

rows.source: Now in its seventh year, the Global Citizen Festival will see tens of thousands of people flock to Central Park's Great Lawn to not only enjoy acts such as Janet Jackson, Cardi B and Shawn Mendes, but also to raise awareness for the event's true goal of ending extreme poverty by 2030.
rows.output: Ugbu a n'afọ nke asaa, ememme Global Citizen ga-ahụ ọtụtụ puku mmadụ na-aga n'ogige Great Lawn nke Central Park ka ha ghara naanị ịnụ ụtọ ihe ngosi dị ka Janet Jackson, Cardi B na Shawn Mendes, kama ka ha mee ka a mara ihe bụ ebe ebumnobi nke mmemme ahụ bụ ị kwụsị ịda ogbenye nke ukwuu site n'afọ 2030.
rows.reference: Ugbu a n’afọ nke asaa ya, Global Citizen Festival ga-ahụ puku kwụrụ puku mmadụ ga-ezute na Ama Central Park, nke abụghị naanị inweta ọṅụ n’ihe nkiri ndị a dịka Janet Jackson, Cardi B, Shawn Mendes, ma ka ha kwalitekwa mmata ezigbo ebumnuche mmemme ịkwụsị ụbịam na 2030.

rows.source: The Global Citizen Festival, which stated in 2012, is an extension of the Global Poverty Project, an international advocacy group hoping to end poverty by increasing the number of people actively fighting against it.
rows.output: Ememme Global Citizen, nke malitere na 2012, bụ mgbọrọgwụ nke Project Global Poverty, otu ndị na-eme ihe n'ụwa niile na-achọ ị kwụsị ịda ogbenye site n'ịbawanye ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị na-alụ ọgụ megide ya.
rows.reference: Global Citizen Festival nke kwuputara na 2012, bụ alaka nke Global Poverty Project, otu nkwalite amụma mba ụwa nwere olile anya ịkwụsị ụbịam site na ịbawanye ọnụọgụ ndị na-alụso ya ọgụ.

rows.source: In order to receive a free ticket for the event (unless you were willing to pay for a VIP ticket), concertgoers had to complete a series of tasks, or "actions" such volunteering, emailing a world leader, making a phone call or any other meaningful ways to help raise awareness of their goal of ending poverty.
rows.output: Iji nweta tiketi n'efu maka mmemme ahụ (ma ọ bụrụ na ị nwere ike ịkwụ ụgwọ maka tiketi VIP), ndị na-ege egwu ga-emecha usoro ọrụ, ma ọ bụ "omume" dị ka inye onyinye, izipu ozi-e nye onye isi ụwa, ime oku ekwentị ma ọ bụ ihe ọ bụla ọzọ nwere ihe dị mkpa iji nyere aka mee ka a mara ihe ha chọrọ ime bụ ịkwatu ịda ogbenye.
rows.reference: Ka ị were nweta tịketị n’efu maka mmemme ahụ (beluso ma ọ masịrị gị ịkwụ ụgwọ tịketị), ndị ga-abịa ihe nkiri a ga-arụ ụfọdụ ọrụ, ma ọ bụ ‘mee ihe’ dịka nwepụta onwe n’ọrụ, izigara onye isi obodo ozi ịntanetị, ịkpọ oku ekwentị ma ọ bụ ụzọ ọ bụla bara uru iji were kpalite mmata ebumnuche ha ịkwụsị ụbịam.

rows.source: But just how successful has Global Citizen been with 12 years left to achieve its goal?
rows.output: Ma, kedụ ka Global Citizen si mee nke ọma n'afọ iri na abụọ fọdụrụ imezu ebumnuche ya?
rows.reference: Mana, kedu ka o si agara Global Citizen nke ọma ebe ha nwere naanị afọ 12 imejuputa ebumnuche ya?

rows.source: Is the idea of rewarding people with a free concert a genuine way to persuade people to demand a call for action, or just another case of so-called "clicktivism" - people feeling like they are making a true difference by signing an online petition or sending a tweet?
rows.output: Ọ bụ echiche nke inye ndị mmadụ ihe nrite n'ụdị egwu n'efu ụzọ ezigbo ụzọ iji mee ka ndị mmadụ chọọ ihe? Ma ọ bụ naanị ihe ọzọ nke a na-akpọ "clicktivism" - ndị mmadụ na-eche na ha na-eme nnukwu ihe site n'ịbanye akwụkwọ n'Ịntanet ma ọ bụ izipu tweet?
rows.reference: Echiche inye ndị mmadụ tịketị n’efu, a bụ ụzọ ziri ezi iji kwanye ndị mmadụ ka ha kpọọ oku mmepụta ihe, ka ọ bụ naanị ụzọ ọzọ ihe akpọrọ “kliktivizm” - ndị chere na ha nwere ihe pụrụ iche ha na-eme n’ezie site na ibinye aka na mkpesa ịntanetị ma ọ bụ zipu tweet?

rows.source: Since 2011, Global Citizen says it has recorded more than 19 million "actions" from its supporters, pushing for a host of different goals.
rows.output: N'afọ 2011, Global Citizen kwuru na o dekọrọ ihe karịrị nde 19 "omume" site n'aka ndị nkwado ya, na-akwalite maka ọtụtụ ebumnuche dị iche iche.
rows.reference: Kemgbe 2011, Global Citizen kwuru na ha enweela ”mmepụta ihe” nde 19 site n’aka ndị nkwado ya, na-akwa maka mmezu ebumnuche dị iche iche.

rows.source: It says that these actions have helped spur world leaders to announce commitments and policies equating to more than $37 billion that is set to affect the lives of more than 2.25 billion people by 2030.
rows.output: Ọ na-ekwu na omume ndị a enyerela aka kpalie ndị isi ụwa ka ha kwupụta nkwa na amụma na ha ga-adị ka ihe karịrị ijeri $37 bụ nke ga-emetụta ihe karịrị ijeri mmadụ 2.25 site na 2030.
rows.reference: O kwuru na mmepụta ihe ndị a enyerela aka mee ndị na-achị achị na mba ụwa ka ha maa ọkwa nkwa yana amụma ruru ihe karịrị ijeri $37, nke ga-emetụta ndụ mmadụ karịrị ijeri 2.25 na 2030.

rows.source: In early 2018, the group cited 390 commitments and announcements stemming from its actions, at least $10 billion of which have already been disbursed or fundraised.
rows.output: N'isi 2018, otu ahụ kwuru na ha nwere 390 nkwekọrịta na 39 nkwupụta sitere na omume ha, opekempe ijeri $10 nke nke a ekesala ma ọ bụ kpọkọta ya.
rows.reference: Na mbido 2018, otu ahụ rụtụrụ aka nkwa na ọkwa 390 nke malitere site na mmepụta ihe ya, opekempe ijeri $10 bụ nke ekesagoro ma ọ bụ tụta n’ego.

rows.source: The group estimates the secured funds have so far made a direct impact on nearly 649 million people across the world.
rows.output: Otu ndị ahụ na-atụ aro na ego ndị a na-echebeela enweela mmetụta ozugbo n'ihe dị ka nde mmadụ 649 n'ofe ụwa.
rows.reference: Otu ahụ na-ama amụma n’ego ndị echekwabara emetụtala n’ahụ mmadụ ruru nde 649 n’ụwa gbaa gburugburu.

rows.source: Some of the key commitments include The Power of Nutrition, a U.K. based partnership of investors and implementers committed to "helping children grow to their full potential," promising to provide Rwanda with $35 million to help end malnutrition in the county after receiving more than 4,700 tweets from Global Citizens.
rows.output: Ụfọdụ n'ime nkwekọrịta ndị dị mkpa gụnyere Ike nri, bụ njikọ nke ndị na-etinye ego na ndị na-eme ihe na UK, na-etinye aka na "inyere ụmụaka aka itolite ruo ikike ha," na-ekwe nkwa inye Rwanda nde $35 iji nyere aka kwụsị erighị nri na obodo ahụ mgbe ha nwetara ihe karịrị 4,700 tweet sitere na ndị obodo ụwa.
rows.reference: Ụfọdụ nkwa ndị ekwere tinyere Power of Nutrition, mmekọrịta ndị ego nkwado dị na U.K yana ndị ntinye n’ọrụ wepụtara onwe ha “inyere ụmụaka aka itozu etozu ihe ha ga-abụ,” na-ekwe Rwanda nkwa nde $35 iji nyere ha aka kwụsị erighị nri na-edozi ahụ dị n’obodo ahụ ka ha nwetachara tweet karịrị 4,700 sitere na Global Citizen.

rows.source: "With support from the UK government, donors, national governments, and Global Citizens just like you, we can make the social injustice of undernutrition a footnote in history," The Power of Nutrition ambassador Tracey Ullman told the crowd during a live concert in London in April 2018.
rows.output: "Na nkwado sitere n'aka gọọmentị UK, ndị na-enye onyinye, gọọmentị mba, na ndị obodo ụwa dị ka gị, anyị nwere ike ime ikpe na-adịghị mma nke erighị nri nke ọma bụrụ akwụkwọ akụkọ n'akụkọ ihe mere eme," onye nnọchi anya Power of Nutrition bụ Tracey Ullman gwara igwe mmadụ n'oge egwu dị ndụ na London n'ọnwa Eprel afọ 2018.
rows.reference: “Na nkwado sitere na gọọmentị UK, ndị na-enye onyinye na gọọmentị mba ọzọ, na Global Citizen dịka gị, anyị ga-eme mmeremme ezighi ezi nke erizughị nri na-edozi ahụ ka ọ bụrụ ozi mgbakwunye na hịstrị.” Onye nnọchi anya Power of Nutrition Tracey Ullman gwara igwe mmadụ n’oge emume egwu na London na Eprel 2018.

rows.source: The group also said that after more than 5,000 actions were taken calling on the U.K. improve nutrition for mothers and children, the government announced funding for a project, the Power of Nutrition, that will reach 5 million women and children with nutrition interventions.
rows.output: Otu ahụ kwuru na ka e mesịrị ihe karịrị 5,000 omume e mere na-arịọ gọọmentị U.K ka ha melite nri maka ndị nne na ụmụaka, gọọmentị kwupụtara ego maka ọrụ, ike nke nri, nke ga-eru 5 nde ụmụ nwanyị na ụmụaka na mmata nri.
rows.reference: Otu ahụ kwukwara nke a ka emechara ihe mmepụta 5,000, na-akpọ U.K oku ka ha meziwanye nri ndozi ahụ maka ndị nne na ụmụaka, gọọmentị mara ọkwa inye ego maka ọrụ, Power of Nutrition, nke ga-eji enyemaka nri ndozi ahụ rute ụmụ-nwanyị na ụmụaka nde 5 aka.

rows.source: In response to one of the FAQs on its website asking "what makes you think we can end extreme poverty?"
rows.output: N'ịza ajụjụ a na webụsaịtị ya na-ajụ "gịnị mere ị ji chee na anyị nwere ike kwụsị ịda ogbenye dị oke njọ?"
rows.reference: N’azịza otu n’ime FAQ dị na ịntanetị ya, na-ajụ, “kedu ihe mere iji chee na anyị nwere ike ịkwụsị oke ụbịam?”

rows.source: Global citizen replied: "It'll be a long and hard path - sometimes we will fall and fail.
rows.output: Onye obodo zuru ụwa ọnụ zara: "Ọ ga-abụ ụzọ dị ogologo na nke siri ike - mgbe ụfọdụ, anyị ga-ada na ịda.
rows.reference: Global Citizen zara: “Ọ ga-abụ ụzọ tere aka ma sie ike - mgbe ụfọdụ anyị ga ada ma daa mba.

rows.source: But, like the great civil rights and anti-apartheid movements before us, we will succeed, because we are more powerful together.
rows.output: Ma, dị ka nnukwu mmegharị ikike obodo na megide ịkpa ókè gara aga, anyị ga-emecha, n'ihi na anyị na-esiwanye ike mgbe anyị jikọtara ọnụ.
rows.reference: Mana, dị ka oke ndọrọndọrọ ikike dịịrị mmadụ yana mmegide ịkpa oke mere tupu anyị, anyị ga-emeri, n’ihi na anyị siri ike karịa ma ejikọọ ọnụ.

rows.source: Janet Jackson, the Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe are among some of the acts performing at this year's event in New York, which will be hosted by Deborra-Lee Furness and Hugh Jackman.
rows.output: Janet Jackson, The Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe bụ ụfọdụ n'ime ndị na-eme ihe ngosi na mmemme a n'afọ a na New York, nke Deborra-Lee Furness na Hugh Jackman ga-ahọpụta.
rows.reference: Janet Jackson,The Weeknd, Shawn Mendes, Cardi B, Janelle Monáe bụ otu n’ime ndị ga-eme ihe nkiri na mmemme nke afọ a na New York, bụ nke Deborra-Lee Furness na Hugh Jackman ga-achịkọba.

rows.source: US could use Navy for "blockade" to hamper Russian energy exports - Interior Secretary
rows.output: US nwere ike iji Navy mee "ngọngọ" iji belata mbupụ mmanụ Russia - Secretary nke ime obodo
rows.reference: US nwere ike iji Ndị Agha Mmiri maka “mgbachi” were gbochie nbufe ahịa Ike ndị Russia- Ọde Akwụkwọ Obodo

rows.source: Washington can "if necessary" resort to its Navy to prevent Russian energy hitting the markets, including in the Middle East, US Internal Secretary Ryan Zinke has revealed, as cited by Washington Examiner.
rows.output: N'ụzọ dị mkpa, Washington nwere ike "ịdaberekwu na ndị agha mmiri ya iji gbochie mmanụ Rọshịa na-abanye n'ahịa, gụnyere n'ebe Ọwụwa Anyanwụ, onye na-ahụ maka ime obodo US bụ Ryan Zinke kwuru, dị ka Washington Examiner si kwuo.
rows.reference: Washington nwere ike “ma ọ dị mkpa” jiri Ndị Agha Mmiri ha nwere gbachie ike Russia ibanye ahịa, tinyere Middle East, Ọde Akwụkwọ US Ryan Zinke kwuputara, dịka arụtụrụ aka na Washington Examiner.

rows.source: Zinke alleged that Russia's engagement in Syria - notably, where it is operating at the invitation of the legitimate government - is a pretext to explore new energy markets.
rows.output: Zinke kwuru na Russia na-etinye aka na Syria - karịsịa, ebe ọ na-arụ ọrụ n'oge ọchịchị dị nsọ - bụ ihe mkpuchi iji nyochaa ahịa mmanụ ọhụrụ.
rows.reference: Zinke boro ebubo na itinye aka nke Russia na Syria - nke ama ama, bụ ebe ọ na-arụ ọrụ n’ihi akpọmoku nke gọọmentị ziri ezi - bụ ụzọ aghụghọ iji nyochaa ahịa ike ọhụrụ.

rows.source: "I believe the reason they are in the Middle East is they want to broker energy just like they do in eastern Europe, the southern belly of Europe," he has reportedly said.
rows.output: "Ekwenyere m na ihe kpatara ha nọ n'ebe Ọwụwa Anyanwụ bụ na ha chọrọ ime ka ha na-enye mmanụ dị ka ha na-eme na Eastern Europe, n'akụkụ ndịda nke Europe," ka o kwuru dị ka akụkọ si kwuo.
rows.reference: “Ekwenyere m n’ihe kpatara ha jiri nọrọ na Middle East bụ ka ha zụọ ahịa ike dị ka ha na-eme na ọwụwa anyanwụ Europe, mgbada Europe,” o kwuru nke a.

rows.source: And, according to to the official, there are ways and means to tackle it.
rows.output: Na, dị ka onye isi, e nwere ụzọ na ụzọ isi mee ya.
rows.reference: Ma, dabere na onye ọrụ ahụ, enwere ụzọ na ka-esi agba ya mgba.

rows.source: "The United States has that ability, with our Navy, to make sure the sea lanes are open, and, if necessary, to blockade, to make sure that their energy does not go to market," he said.
rows.output: "United States nwere ike ahụ, na Navy anyị, iji hụ na ụzọ mmiri na-emeghe, na, ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mkpa, iji gbochie, iji hụ na mmanụ ha anaghị aga n'ahịa," ka o kwuru.
rows.reference: “United States nwere ike, jiri Ndị Agha Mmiri anyị, hụ na okporo ụzọ mmiri anyị ghe oghe, ma ọ bụrụ na ọ dị mkpa, gbachie, iji hụ na ike ha abaghị ahịa.” o kwuru.

rows.source: Zinke was addressing the attendees of the event hosted by the Consumer Energy Alliance, a non-profit group which styles itself as the "voice of the energy consumer" in the US.
rows.output: Zinke na-ekwu okwu ndị bịaranụ nke mmemme a na-eme site na Consumer Energy Alliance, otu na-abụghị nke na-eme ihe na-eme ka ọ bụrụ "olu nke onye na-eri ike" na US.
rows.reference: Zinke na-agwa ndị bịara emume ndị Consumer Energy Alliance chịkọbara, otu anaghị achọ uru nke dobere onwe ya dịka “olu ndị na-eri ike” na US.

rows.source: He went to compare Washington's approaches to dealing with Russia and Iran, noting that they are effectively the same.
rows.output: Ọ gara ileba anya n'ụzọ Washington si eme ihe gbasara Russia na Iran, na-ekwu na ha bụ otu ihe ahụ.
rows.reference: Ọ gara tulee usoro Washington ji emeso Russia na Iran omume, chọpụta na ha abụọ bụ otu.

rows.source: "The economic option on Iran and Russia is, more or less, leveraging and replacing fuels," he said, while referring to Russia as a "one trick pony" with an economy dependent on fossil fuels.
rows.output: "Nhọrọ akụ na ụba na Iran na Russia bụ, n'ụzọ dị ukwuu, iji na dochie mmanụ," ka o kwuru, mgbe ọ na-ezo aka na Russia dị ka "ịnyịnya otu aghọta" nwere akụ na ụba dabere na mmanụ.
rows.reference: “Nhọrọ akụnụba Iran na Russia bụ, dabere naanị, ịgbazinye na iweghachi mmanụ ọkụ ụgbọ ala,” o kwuru, ebe ọ na-arụtụ Russia aka dị ka “ọgba otu egwu” nwere akụnụba dabere na mmanụ ọkụ na unyi ekereụwa.

rows.source: The statements come as Trump administration has been on a mission to boost the export of its liquefied natural gas to Europe, replacing Russia, the far cheaper option for European consumers.
rows.output: Nkwupụta ndị a bịarutere ka ọchịchị Trump na-agbalịsi ike ịbawanye mbupụ gas nke a na-eme ka ọ dị nro na Europe, iji dochie Russia, nhọrọ dị ọnụ ala maka ndị na-azụ ahịa Europe.
rows.reference: Nkwuputa ndị a pụtara ka ọchịchị Trump na-agbalị ịkwalite ibufe ahịa mmiri gaasị ọnatarachi ha na Europe, ịnọchi Russia, bụ nke ka dị ọnụala maka ndị na-eri ahịa nke Europe.

rows.source: For that effect, the Trump administration officials, including US President Donald Trump himself, try to persuade Germany to pull out of the "inappropriate" Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, which according to Trump, made Berlin Moscow's "captive."
rows.output: Maka nke ahụ, ndị ọrụ ọchịchị Trump, gụnyere Onye isi ala US Donald Trump n'onwe ya, na-agbalị ime ka Germany pụọ na "ihe na-adịghị mma" Nord Stream 2 pipeline project, nke dị ka Trump si kwuo, mere Berlin ka ọ bụrụ "ndị na-ejide" Moscow.
rows.reference: Maka imezu nke a, ndị ọrụ ọchịchị Trump tinyere Onye Isi Ala US Donald Trump n’onwe ya, na-agbalị ịkwanye Germany ka ọ pụta na atụmatụ ọwa mmiri Nord Stream 2 “adịghị mma”, bụ nke dabere na Trump, mere Berlin “onye nke Moscow ji eji.

rows.source: Moscow has repeatedly stressed that the $11 billion Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which is set to double the existing pipeline capacity to 110 billion cubic meters, is a purely economic project.
rows.output: Moscow na-emegharị ugboro ugboro na $11 ijeri Nord Stream 2 pipeline, nke ga-eme ka ikike pipeline dị ugbu a dịkwuo elu na 110 ijeri cubic mita, bụ naanị ọrụ akụ na ụba.
rows.reference: Moscow ekwuola ugboro ugboro na ijeri $11 ọwa mmiri Nord Stream 2 ahụ, bụ nke emebere ka o bulie ike ọwa mmiri nke dị adị ruo ijeri 110 kubik mita, bụ naanị atụmatụ maka akụnụba.

rows.source: The Kremlin argues that Washington's fervent opposition to the project is simply driven by economic reasons and is an example of unfair competition.
rows.output: Ụlọ Kremlin na-ekwu na Washington na-emegide ọrụ ahụ nke ukwuu bụ naanị n'ihi ihe gbasara akụ na ụba na ọ bụ ihe atụ nke asọmpi na-ezighị ezi.
rows.reference: Kremlin na-arụ ụka na oke mgbachi nke Washington n’atụmatụ ahụ bụ naanị n’ihi akụnụba bụ ihe kpatara ya ma bụrụ ọmụmatụ asompi n’adịghị mma.

rows.source: "I believe we share the view that energy cannot be a tool to exercise pressure and that consumers should be able to choose the suppliers," Russian Energy Minister Aleksandr Novak said following a meeting with US Energy Secretary Rick Perry in Moscow in September.
rows.output: "Ekwenyere m na anyị na-ekwukwa na ike enweghị ike iji ya mee ka ndị na-azụ ahịa nwee nrụgide ma ndị na-azụ ahịa kwesịrị inwe ike ịhọrọ ndị na-enye ha." Onye Minisita na-ahụ maka ike nke Russia bụ Aleksandr Novak kwuru mgbe ọ zutere onye minisita na-ahụ maka ike nke US bụ Rick Perry na Moscow na Septemba.
rows.reference: “Ekwenyere m na anyị na-ahụkọrịta na ike enweghị ike ịbụ ngwaọrụ eji eme nkwanye, ndị na-eri ahịa kwesịrị ịhọrọ onye mbunye ahịa ya,” Mịnịsta Ike nke Russia Aleksandr Novak kwuru, sotere nnọkọ ya na Ọde Akwụkwọ Ike nke US Rick Perry na Moscow na Septemba.

rows.source: The US stance has drawn backlash from Germany, which has reaffirmed its commitment to the project.
rows.output: Mmetụta US ahụ enwetala azịza site n'aka Germany, bụ́ nke kwughachiri nkwenye ya n'ọrụ ahụ.
rows.reference: Ọnọdụ US ebutela nkwụtọ si Germany, bụ nke kwuputakwara nkwado ha n’atụmatụ ahụ.

rows.source: Germany's leading organization for industry, the Federation of German Industries (BDI), has called on the US to stay away from the EU energy policy and the bilateral agreements between Berlin and Moscow.
rows.output: Otu ndị isi ụlọ ọrụ na Germany, Federation of German Industries (BDI), akpọọla United States ka ha ghara itinye aka na amụma ike nke EU na nkwekọrịta abụọ dị n'etiti Berlin na Moscow.
rows.reference: Ụlọ ọrụ na-achị na Germany maka ụlọ nrụpụta ihe, Federation of German Industries (BDI), akpọkuola US ka ha wepu aka na amụma ike nke Europe yana nkwekọrịta obodo na obodo dị n’etiti Berlin na Moscow.

rows.source: "I have a big problem when a third state interferes in our energy supply," Dieter Kempf, head of the Federation of German Industries (BDI) said following a recent meeting between German Chancellor Angela Merkel and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
rows.output: "Enwere m nnukwu nsogbu mgbe steeti nke atọ na-etinye aka na inye anyị ọkụ eletrik," Dieter Kempf, onye isi ụlọ ọrụ Federation of German Industries (BDI) kwuru mgbe ọ gara nzukọ dị nso n'etiti Chancellor German Angela Merkel na President Russia Vladimir Putin.
rows.reference: “Enwere m nnukwu nsogbu mgbe obodo nke atọ n’etinye anya na mbunye ahịa ike anyị,” Dieter Kempf onye isi Federation of German Industries (BDI) kwuru, sotere nnọkọ dị n’etiti German Chancellor Angela Merkel na Onye Isi Ala Vladmir Putin.

rows.source: Elizabeth Warren Will Take "Hard Look" At Running For President in 2020, Massachusetts Senator Says
rows.output: Elizabeth Warren ga-elele "nleba anya siri ike" na ịgba ọsọ maka Onye isi ala na 2020, onye omebe iwu Massachusetts kwuru.
rows.reference: Elizabeth Warren “Ga-elebe Anya Nke Ukwuu” Na Ịzọ Maka Onye Isi Ala na 2020, Onye Ọmebe Iwu Massachusetts Kwuru

rows.source: Massachusetts Senator Elizabeth Warren said on Saturday she would take a "hard look" at running for president following the midterm elections.
rows.output: Onye nnọchi anya Massachusetts bụ Elizabeth Warren kwuru na Satọde na ọ ga-eleba anya n'ịzụrụ onye isi ala mgbe ntuli aka etiti gasịrị.
rows.reference: Onye ọmebe iwu Massachusettes Elizabeth Warren kwuru na Satọde na ya “ga-elebe anya nke ukwuu” ịzọ maka onye isi ala, sotere ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị.

rows.source: During a town hall in Holyoke, Massachusetts, Warren confirmed she'd consider running.
rows.output: N'oge ọgbakọ obodo dị na Holyoke, Massachusetts, Warren kwadoro na ọ ga-atụle ịgba ọsọ.
rows.reference: N’oge nzụkọ obodo na Holyoke, Massachusetts, Warren kwuputakwara na ya ga-atule ịzọ ọkwa.

rows.source: "It's time for women to go to Washington and fix our broken government and that includes a woman at the top," she said, according to The Hill.
rows.output: "Oge eruola ka ụmụ nwanyị gaa Washington ma dozie gọọmentị anyị gbawara agbawa ma ọ gụnyere nwanyị n'elu," ka o kwuru, dị ka The Hill si kwuo.
rows.reference: “O ruola oge ụmụ-nwanyị ga-aga na Washington were jee dozie gọọmentị anyị mebiri emebi, bụ nke tinyere ụmụ-nwanyị ịnọ n’isi.” o kwuru, dabere na The Hill.

rows.source: "After November 6, I will take a hard look at running for president."
rows.output: "Ka ọnwa Nọvemba 6 gachara, m ga-eleba anya nke ọma n'ịzụlite maka onye isi ala."
rows.reference: “Nọvemba 6 gachaa, A ga-elebe anya nke ukwuu n’ịzọ maka onye isi ala.”

rows.source: Warren weighed in on President Donald Trump during the town hall, saying he was "taking this county in the wrong direction.
rows.output: Warren kwuru okwu banyere Onye isi ala Donald Trump n'oge nnọkọ obodo ahụ, na-ekwu na ọ na-eme ka obodo ahụ "ga n'ụzọ na-ezighị ezi."
rows.reference: Warren tinyere ọnụ na Onye Isi Ala Donald Trump n’ime oge nzụkọ obodo ahụ, na-ekwu na ọ “na-eduba obodo a n’ụzọ adịghị mma.

rows.source: "I am worried down to my bones about what Donald Trump is doing to our democracy," she said.
rows.output: "Ana m ejighị n'aka ruo n'okpokoro m gbasara ihe Donald Trump na-eme na ọchịchị onye kwuo uche ya," ka o kwuru.
rows.reference: “Uche na-eche m ruo n’ọkpụkpụ banyere ihe Donald Trump na-eme ọchịchị onye kwuo uche ya nke anyị,” o kwuru.

rows.source: Warren has been outspoken in her criticism of Trump and his Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh.
rows.output: Warren enyela okwu n'okwu ya na Trump na onye a họpụtara ya n'ụlọikpe Kasị Elu, Brett Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: Warren na-ekwuwapụta nkọcha ya maka Trump yana onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ya, Brett Kavanaugh.

rows.source: In a tweet on Friday, Warren said "of course we need an FBI investigation before voting."
rows.output: N'ime tweet na Fraịde, Warren kwuru "n'ezie anyị chọrọ nyocha FBI tupu anyị eme ntuli aka."
rows.reference: Na tweet Fraịde Warren kwuru ”n’ezie anyị chọrọ nyocha FBI tupu ntuli aka.”

rows.source: A poll released on Thursday, however, showed a majority of Warren's own constituents do not think she should run in 2020.
rows.output: Ntụle e wepụtara na Tọzdee, n'agbanyeghị, gosiri na ọtụtụ n'ime ndị na-ahụ maka ọchịchị Warren anaghị eche na ọ ga-azọ ọkwa na 2020.
rows.reference: Nyocha ewepụtara na Tọsde, kosiladị, gosiri ọtụtụ ndị okpuru ọchịchị ntuli aka nke Warren echeghị na ọ kwesịrị ịzọ ọkwa na 2020.

rows.source: Fifty-eight percent of "likely" Massachusetts voters said the senator should not run, according to the Suffolk University Political Research Center/Boston Globe poll.
rows.output: Puku ise na iri ise na asatọ pasent nke ndị na-atụ anya na ha ga-eme ntuli aka Massachusetts kwuru na onye sinetọ ahụ ekwesịghị ịzọ ọkwa, dị ka nyocha nke Suffolk University Political Research Center/Boston Globe mere.
rows.reference: Pesentị Iri ise na asatọ nke “ndị nwere ike” ime ntuli aka nke Massachusetts kwuru na ọmebe iwu ahụ ekwesịghị ịzọ ọkwa, dabere na nyocha nke Suffolk University Poilitical Research Center/Boston Globe.

rows.source: Thirty-two percent supported such a run.
rows.output: Puku iri atọ na abụọ pasentị kwadoro ịrụ ọrụ dị otú ahụ.
rows.reference: Pesentị Iri atọ na abụọ kwadoro yabụ ịzọ ọkwa.

rows.source: The poll showed more support for a run by former Governor Deval Patrick, with 38 percent supporting a potential run and 48 percent against it.
rows.output: Nleba anya ahụ gosiri na ọ nwere nkwado karịa maka ịgba ọsọ nke onye bụbu gọvanọ Deval Patrick, ebe 38 pasent na-akwado ịga n'ihu na 48 pasent na-emegide ya.
rows.reference: Nyocha ahụ gosiri nkwado karịa maka ịzọ ọkwa nke Governor Deval Patrick chịburu ọchịchị, nke nwere pesentị 38 na-akwado ya ịzọ ọkwa ebe pesentị 48 megidere ya.

rows.source: Other high profile Democratic names discussed in regard to a potential 2020 run include former Vice President Joe Biden and Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders.
rows.output: Ndị ọzọ a ma ama nke ndị Democrats a kpọrọ aha n'ihe gbasara ọsọ 2020 gụnyere onye bụbu osote onye isi ala Joe Biden na onye sinetọ Vermont Bernie Sanders.
rows.reference: Aha ndị Demokrat ndị ukwuu ekwutere banyere ịzọ ọkwa nke 2020 tinyere Osote Onye Isi Ala Joe Biden chịburu ọchịchị na Onye Ọmebe iwu Vermont Bernie Sanders.

rows.source: Biden said he would decide officially by January, the Associated Press reported.
rows.output: Biden kwuru na ya ga-ekpebi ya n'ụzọ gọọmentị n'ọnwa Jenụwarị, dị ka Associated Press si kwuo.
rows.reference: Biden kwuru na ya ga-eme mkpebi nke ya na Jenuarị, Associated Press kwuputara.

rows.source: Sarah Palin cites Track Palin's PTSD at Donald Trump rally
rows.output: Sarah Palin na-ekwu na Track Palin's PTSD na nzukọ Donald Trump
rows.reference: Sarah Palin rụtụrụ aka na PTSD Track Palin na nnọkọ ndọrọndọrọ Donald Trump.

rows.source: Track Palin, 26, spent a year in Iraq after enlisting on Sept.
rows.output: Track Palin, 26, nọrụ afọ otu n'Iraq ka o tinyere aka na Septemba.
rows.reference: Track Palin, 26, nọrọ otu afọ na Iraq ka ọ banyechara na Sept.

rows.source: He was arrested and charged in a domestic violence incident on Monday night
rows.output: E jidere ya, kpọọ ya ikpe n'ihe gbasara ime ihe ike n'ụlọ n'uhuruchi Mọnde
rows.reference: Anwudoro ya wee gbaa ya akwụkwọ maka ime ihe ike n’ụlọ n’abalị Mọnde

rows.source: "What my own son is going through, what he is going through coming back, I can relate to other families who feel ramifications of PTSD and some of the woundedness that our soldiers do return with," she told the audience at a rally for Donald Trump in Tulsa, Oklahoma.
rows.output: "Kedu ihe nwa m nwoke na-aga, ihe ọ na-aga na-alọta, m nwere ike ịghọta ndị ezinụlọ ndị ọzọ na-enwe mmetụta nke PTSD na ụfọdụ mmerụ ahụ ndị agha anyị na-alọta," o kwuru ndị na-ege ntị n'ọgbako maka Donald Trump na Tulsa, Oklahoma.
rows.reference: “Ihe nwa m nwoke na-agabiga, ihe ọ na-agabiga na nlaghachi azụ, Enwere m ike inwe nghọta ezinụlọ ndị ọzọ n’ahụ nsonazụ PTSD yana ụfọdụ ihe mmerụ ahụ ndị agha anyị na-eji alata,” ọ gwara ndị nọ na nnọkọ ndọrọndọrọ a maka Donald Trump na Tulsa, Oklahoma.

rows.source: Palin called his arrest "the elephant in the room" and said of her son and other war veterans, "they come back a bit different, they come back hardened, they come back wondering if there is that respect for what it is that their fellow soldiers and airmen, and every other member of the military, has given to the country."
rows.output: Palin kpọrọ nkwusioru ya "ọkụlù dị n'ime ụlọ" ma kwuo banyere nwa ya nwoke na ndị agha agha ndị ọzọ, "ha na-alọta ntakịrị dị iche, ha na-alọta ike, ha na-alọta na-eche ma ọ bụ na e nwere nsọpụrụ maka ihe ọ bụ na ndị agha ha na ndị agha ha, na onye ọ bụla ọzọ nọ n'ọrụ agha, nyere obodo ahụ."
rows.reference: Palin kpọrọ nwudo ya ‘enyi nọ n’ime ụlọ” wee kwuo maka nwa ya nwoke na ndị ọzọ gara agha, ha na-alaghachi azụ dị obere iche, ha na-alaghachi azụ nwee obi ike, ha na-alaghachi na-ajụ ma enwere nsọpụrụ enwere maka ndị agha ibe ya, ndị agha ikuku, na ndị ọ bụla nọ n’otu ndị agha, n’ihe ha nyegoro obodo ha.”

rows.source: He was arrested on Monday in Wasilla, Alaska, and charged with domestic violence assault on a female, interfering with a report of domestic violence and possession of a weapon while intoxicated, according to Dan Bennett, a spokesman for the Wasilla Police Department.
rows.output: E jidere ya na Mọnde n'Wasilla, Alaska, ma bo ya ebubo na ọ na-emegbu nwanyị n'ụlọ, na igbochi akụkọ banyere ime ihe ike n'ụlọ na inwe ngwa agha mgbe ọ na-aṅụ mmanya, dị ka Dan Bennett, onye na-ekwu okwu maka ndị uwe ojii Wasilla si kwuo.
rows.reference: Anwudoro ya na Mọnde na Wasilla, Alaska, wee gbaa ya akwụkwọ maka imeso nwanyị ihe ike n’ụlọ, mgbochi na mkpesa nke ime ihe ike n’ụlọ yana iji ngwa ọgụ ka oriri ihe na-egbu egbu, dabere na Dan Bennett, onye nkwuchite okwu ndị Wasilla Police Department.

rows.source: 18 states, D.C. support challenge to new asylum policy
rows.output: 18 steeti, D.C. na-akwado ihe ịma aka na amụma ụlọ mkpọrọ ọhụrụ
rows.reference: Obodo 18, D.C na-akwado ịche aka mgba nke amụma mgbata ọsọ ndụ ọhụrụ

rows.source: Eighteen states and the District of Columbia are supporting a legal challenge to a new U.S. policy that denies asylum to victims fleeing gang or domestic violence.
rows.output: Puku iri na asatọ na mpaghara Columbia na-akwado ihe ịma aka iwu megide amụma U.S. ọhụrụ nke na-ajụ ndị na-agbanarị ime ihe ike n'ime ụlọ ma ọ bụ ime ihe ike n'ime ụlọ.
rows.reference: Obodo iri na asatọ yana District of Colombia na-akwado ịche aka mgba n’ụzọ iwu nke amụma U.S ọhụrụ nke anaghị enye nchekwa maka ndị na-agbata ọsọ ndụ n’ihi otu ndị ike ma ọ bụ ihe ike ime ụlọ.

rows.source: Representatives from the 18 states and the district filed a friend-of-the-court brief Friday in Washington to support an asylum-seeker challenging the policy, NBC News reported.
rows.output: Ndị nnọchi anya steeti iri na asatọ na mpaghara ahụ degaara ụlọikpe akwụkwọ enyemaka nke ụlọikpe na Fraịde na Washington iji kwado onye na-achọ ebe mgbaba na-eme ihe megide amụma ahụ, NBC News kwuru.
rows.reference: Ndị nnọchi anya si obodo 18 ahụ na district gbara akwụkwọ ndị ọ metụtara inyere aka na Fraịde na Washington iji kwado onye mgbata ọsọ ndụ nke na-echere amụma ahụ aka mgba, NBC News kwuputara.

rows.source: The full name of the plaintiff in the Grace v. Sessions suit that the American Civil Liberties Union filed in August against the federal policy has not been revealed.
rows.output: Akpọrọ aha zuru ezu nke onye na-azọrata n'okwu Grace v. Sessions nke otu American Civil Liberties Union tinyere n'ụzọ na August megide amụma gọọmentị etiti ka a na-ekpugheghị.
rows.reference: Ekwuputabeghị aha ndepụta n’uju nke onye na-agba akwụkwọ n’okwu Grace v. Sessions nke American Civil Liberties Union gbara na Ọgọst megide amụma etiti obodo.

rows.source: She said her partner "and his violent gang member sons," abused her but U.S. officials denied her request for asylum July 20.
rows.output: Ọ sịrị na onye mmekọ ya "na ụmụ nwoke ndị otu ya na-eme ihe ike," na-emegbu ya, mana ndị ọrụ U.S. jụrụ arịrịọ ya maka ebe mgbaba na Julaị 20.
rows.reference: O kwuru na onye ya na ya bi “na ndị otu ike ụmụ ya nwoke” megburu ya, ma ndị ọrụ U.S gbachibidoro arịrịọ ya maka mgbata ọsọ ndụ na Julaị 20.

rows.source: She was detained in Texas.
rows.output: E jidere ya na Texas.
rows.reference: Akpọchiri ya na Texas.

rows.source: The states' attorneys supporting Grace described El Salvador, Honduras and Guatemala, which produce a large number of applicants for U.S. asylum, as nations facing pervasive problems with gangs and domestic violence.
rows.output: Ndị ọka iwu steeti na-akwado Grace kọwara El Salvador, Honduras na Guatemala, bụ́ ndị na-emepụta nnukwu ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị na-achọ mgbaba na U.S., dị ka mba na-eche nsogbu na-agbapụta na ime ihe ike n'ime ụlọ.
rows.reference: Ndị ọka iwu obodo nke na-akwado Grace kọwara na El Salvador, Honduras na Guatemala, mebere ọnụọgụ kacha na ndị na-etinye akwụkwọ maka mgbata ọsọ ndụ na U.S, dịka mba na-alụso ọgụ mbawanye otu ndị ike na ihe ike ime ụlọ.

rows.source: The new U.S. asylum policy reversed a 2014 decision by the Board of Immigrant Appeals that allowed undocumented immigrants fleeing domestic violence to apply for asylum.
rows.output: Mmachi amụma ụlọ ọrụ na-ahụ maka ndị na-achọ mgbaba na U.S. wepụrụ mkpebi 2014 nke Board of Immigrant Appeals nke nyere ndị na-enweghị akwụkwọ ikike na-agbanarị ime ihe ike ohere ịtụpụta mgbaba.
rows.reference: Amụma ọhụrụ nke U.S megharịrị mkpebi 2014 nke Board of Immigrant Appeals mere na-anabata ndị mbịambịa ejighị akwụkwọ na-agba ọsọ ihe ike ime ụlọ itinye akwụkwọ mgbata ọsọ ndụ.

rows.source: District of Columbia Attorney General Karl Racine said in a statement Friday that the new policy "ignores decades of state, federal, and international law."
rows.output: Onye ọka iwu nke District of Columbia, Karl Racine kwuru na nkwupụta Fraịde na amụma ọhụrụ ahụ "na-elegharakarị iri afọ nke iwu steeti, gọọmentị etiti na nke mba ụwa anya."
rows.reference: Onye Isi Ọka Iwu District of Columbia Karl Racine kwuru na nkwuputa Fraịde na amụma ọhụrụ ahụ “n’eleghara anya iwu nke obodo, etiti obodo na mba ofesi nke afọ kwụrụ afọ.”

rows.source: "Federal law requires that all asylum claims be adjudicated on the particular facts and circumstances of the claim, and such a bar violates that principle," the friend-of-the court brief said.
rows.output: Iwu gọọmentị etiti chọrọ ka a na-ekpe ikpe n'ihe gbasara nchekwa nke ndị na-achọ mgbaba, na nke a na-emebi ụkpụrụ ahụ.
rows.reference: “Iwu etiti obodo chọrọ na a ga-eme mkpebi na mkpesa ndị mgbata ọsọ ndụ ọ bụla n’ihe akaebe na ọnọdụ mkpesa ahụ, nke n’ụdị mgbachi ahụ na-emegide usoro iwu ahụ, “ịgba akwụkwọ ndị ọ metụtara inyere aka” kwuru.

rows.source: Attorneys further argued in the brief that the policy denying immigrants entry hurts the U.S. economy, saying they are more likely to become entrepreneurs and "supply necessary labor."
rows.output: Ndị ọka iwu gara n'ihu na-ekwu na akwụkwọ dị mkpirisi na amụma na-ajụ ndị na-abụghị ndị America ịbata na-emerụ akụ na ụba U.S., na-ekwu na ha nwere ike ịbụ ndị na-azụ ahịa na "nye ọrụ dị mkpa."
rows.reference: Ndị ọka iwu gara n’ihu na-arụ ụka n’akwụkwọ ha gbara na amụma ahụ ịgbachi ndị mbịambịa ịbata na-emerụ akụnụba U.S ahụ, na-ekwu na ha na-abụkarị ndị nọrọ onwe ha azụ ahịa ma “na-enye ndị ọrụ ngo achọrọ.”

rows.source: Attorney General Jeff Sessions ordered immigration judges to no longer grant asylum to victims fleeing domestic abuse and gang violence in June.
rows.output: Onye ọka iwu Jeff Sessions nyere iwu ka ndị ọka ikpe mbata na ọpụpụ ghara inye ndị na-agbanarị ime ihe ike n'ụlọ na ime ihe ike n'ìgwè mmadụ n'ụzọ dị mma n'ọnwa June.
rows.reference: Onye Isi Ọka Iwu Jeff Sessions nyere ndị ọka ikpe iwu gbasara ndị mbịambịa, ka ha ghara inyezi nchekwa maka ndị mgbata ọsọ ndụ na-agbanarị mmegbu ihe ike ime ụlọ na otu ndị ike na Juun.

rows.source: "Asylum is available for those who leave their home country because of persecution or fear on account of race, religion, nationality, or membership in a particular social group or political opinion," Sessions said in his June 11 announcement of the policy.
rows.output: "Ụlọ mgbaba dị maka ndị na-ahapụ obodo ha n'ihi mmegide ma ọ bụ egwu n'ihi agbụrụ, okpukpe, mba, ma ọ bụ ịbụ onye otu ìgwè mmadụ ma ọ bụ echiche ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị," Sessions kwuru na 11 June 11.
rows.reference: “Nchekwa mgbata ọsọ ndụ dịịrị ndị na-ahapụ obodo ha n’ihi mkpagbu ma ọ bụ ụjọ n’ihi agbụrụ, okpukpe, obodo onye si, ma ọ bụ nsonye n’otu mmekọrịta ọha ma ọ bụ echiche gbasara ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị,” Sessions kwuru na ịma ọkwa amụma ya na Juun 11.

rows.source: Asylum was never meant to alleviate all problems -- even all serious problems -- that people face every day all over the world.
rows.output: Nchekwube abụghị mgbe a tụrụ anya na ọ ga-eweda nsogbu niile -- ọbụna nsogbu niile -- ndị mmadụ na-eche kwa ụbọchị n'ebe niile n'ụwa.
rows.reference: Emebeghị nchekwa mgbata ọsọ ndụ ka obeleta nsogbu niile enwere - ọbụlagodi nsogbu niile siri ike - nke ndị mmadụ n’ahụ n’ụwa niile.

rows.source: Desperate rescue efforts in Palu as death toll doubles in race to find survivors
rows.output: Mgbalị ịzọpụta ndị gbara ọsọ ndụ na Palu ka ọnụ ọgụgụ ndị nwụrụ na-amụba n'ụzọ dị egwu n'ịhọrọn ndị lanarịrị
rows.reference: Mbọ agwụ ike ịzọpụta ndị gbanarịrị ihe mberede na Palu dịka ọnụọgụ ndị nwụrụ anwụ na-agbago

rows.source: For survivors, the situation was increasingly dire.
rows.output: Maka ndị lanarịrị, ọnọdụ ahụ na-akawanye njọ.
rows.reference: Maka ndị gbanarịrị ihe mberede, ọnọdụ ahụ na-esiwanye ike.

rows.source: "It feels very tense," said 35-year-old mother Risa Kusuma, comforting her feverish baby boy at an evacuation centre in the gutted city of Palu.
rows.output: "Ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-adị m ka ọ na-ad
rows.reference: “Ọ na-adị oke echiche,” Risa Kusuma kwuru, nne nke gbara afọ 35, na-agụgụ nwa nwoke ya na-amajiji n’ebe ndị gbapụrụ ọsọ n’obodo Palu mebiri emebi nọ.

rows.source: "Every minute an ambulance brings in bodies.
rows.output: "Opekempe otu nkeji, ụgbọ ala mgbaka na-ebunye ozu.
rows.reference: “Nkeji ọ bụla ụgbọ ala ihe mberede na-ebute ozu.

rows.source: Clean water is scarce."
rows.output: "O nwere mmiri dị ọcha."
rows.reference: Mmiri dị ọcha dị ụkọ.”

rows.source: Residents were seen returning to their destroyed homes, picking through waterlogged belongings, trying to salvage anything they could find.
rows.output: Ndị bi na ya na-ahụ ka ha na-alọta n'ụlọ ha mebiri emebi, na-ahọrọ ihe ha nwere n'ime ihe ndị mmiri riri, na-agbalị ịzọpụta ihe ọ bụla ha nwere ike ịchọta.
rows.reference: Ahụrụ ndị bi n’obodo ka ha na-alaghachi n’ụlọ ha mebiri emebi, na-atụta ihe n’arịa ndị mmiri juru, na-agbalị ịzọpụta ihe ndị ọ bụla ha nwere ike.

rows.source: Hundreds of people were injured and hospitals, damaged by the magnitude 7.5 quake, were overwhelmed.
rows.output: Puku n'ụzọ n'ụzọ abụọ merụrụ ahụ, ụlọ ọgwụ ndị ahụ, nke oke ala 7.5 ahụ mebiri emebi, juputara.
rows.reference: Narị kwụrụ narị mmadụ merụrụ ahụ na ụlọ ọgwụ nke ala ọmajiji ruru 7.5 mebiri, juputara.

rows.source: Some of the injured, including Dwi Haris, who suffered a broken back and shoulder, rested outside Palu's Army Hospital, where patients were being treated outdoors due to continuing strong aftershocks.
rows.output: Ụfọdụ ndị merụrụ ahụ, gụnyere Dwi Haris, onye merụrụ azụ na ubu, nọdụrụ n'èzí ụlọ ọgwụ ndị agha Palu, ebe ndị ọrịa na-aṅụ ọgwụ n'èzí n'ihi na a ka nwere nnukwu mgbagwojuru.
rows.reference: Ụfọdụ ndị merụrụ ahụ tinyere Dwi Haris, onye nke azụ na ubu ya gbajiri, nọ n’ihu ilo Palu Army Hospital ezu ike, ebe a na-elete ndị merụrụ ahụ n’ilo n’ihi ọmajiji siri ike ka na-aga n’ihu.

rows.source: Tears filled his eyes as he recounted feeling the violent earthquake shake the fifth-floor hotel room he shared with his wife and daughter.
rows.output: Mmiri na-ejupụta anya ya ka ọ na-akọ akụkọ banyere inwe mmetụta nke ala ọma jijiji na-adịghị mma nke mere ka ụlọ nkwari akwụ na ala nke ise nke ya na nwunye ya na nwa ya nwanyị.
rows.reference: Anya mmiri juru ya anya ka ọ na-akọ ka ajọ ala ọmajiji ahụ siri kwaa elu ụlọ nke ise ụlọ nkwari akụ ya na nwunye ya na nwa ya nwanyị nọ.

rows.source: "There was no time to save ourselves.
rows.output: "Ọ dịghị oge iji chekwaa onwe anyị.
rows.reference: “Oghere adịghị ịzọtakwa onwe anyị.

rows.source: I was squeezed into the ruins of the wall, I think," Haris told Associated Press, adding that his family was in town for a wedding.
rows.output: Ejiri m mmanụ n'ime ihe ndị gbara ọsọ ndụ nke mgbidi ahụ, echere m," Haris gwara Associated Press, na-agbakwunye na ezinụlọ ya nọ n'obodo maka agbamakwụkwu.
rows.reference: Echere m na afanyere m n’ime mgbawa dị n’ahụ aja, Harris gwara Associated Press, na-agbakwunye n’ezinụlọ ya batara n’obodo ịga agbamakwụkwọ.

rows.source: "I heard my wife cry for help, but then silence.
rows.output: "Anụrụ m olu nwunye m na-eti mkpu maka enyemaka, ma mgbe ahụ, ọ dị jụụ.
rows.reference: “A nụrụ m ka nwunye m bere akwa maka enyemaka, ọzọ bụ ịda jụụ.

rows.source: I don't know what happened to her and my child.
rows.output: Amaghị m ihe mere ya na nwa m.
rows.reference: Amaghị m ihe mere ya na nwa m.

rows.source: I hope they are safe."
rows.output: "Ana m atụ anya na ha dị mma."
rows.reference: A na m atụ anya na ha nọ nke ọma.”

rows.source: U.S. ambassador accuses China of 'bullying' with 'propaganda ads'
rows.output: Onye nnọchi anya U.S. na-ebo ebubo na China na-eme "mmaja" na "mgbasa ozi mgbasa ozi"
rows.reference: Onye nnọchite anya U.S na-ebo China Ebubo “mmegide” site na ‘mgbasa ozi asị’

rows.source: A week after an official Chinese newspaper ran a four-page ad in a U.S. daily touting the mutual benefits of U.S.-China trade, the U.S. ambassador to China accused Beijing of using the American press to spread propaganda.
rows.output: Otu izu ka akwụkwọ akụkọ gọọmentị China bipụtara akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi peeji anọ n'otu akwụkwọ akụkọ US, onye nnọchi anya US na China boro Beijing ebubo na ọ na-eji mgbasa ozi America gbasaa mgbasa ozi.
rows.reference: Otu izu akwụkwọ akụkọ China buchara ozi n’ibe akwụkwọ anọ n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi U.S na-ekwu maka elele mmekọrịta azụmahịa U.S.-China, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China boro Beijing ebubo iji ndị mgbasa ozi America were ebusa ozi asị.

rows.source: U.S. President Donald Trump last Wednesday referred to the China Daily's paid supplement in the Des Moines Register - the state of Iowa's biggest selling newspaper - after accusing China of seeking to meddle in the Nov. 6 U.S. congressional elections, a charge China denies.
rows.output: Onye isi ala U.S. Donald Trump kwuru na Wednesde gara aga na China Daily na-enye ego na Des Moines Register, akwụkwọ akụkọ kachasị na Iowa, ka ọ na-ebo China ebubo na ha na-agbalị ime ka ntuli aka nke Nov. 6 nke ndị omebe iwu U.S. na-eme, nke China na-ekwu na ha emeghị.
rows.reference: U.S. Onye Isi Ala Donald Trump na Wenesde gara aga rụtụrụ aka na mgbakwunye akwụrụ ụgwọ nke China Daily na Des Moines Register - akwụkwọ akụkọ obodo Iowa kacha ere ahịa - ka o bochara China ebubo ịchọ itinye aka na ntuli aka ndị ọmebe iwu U.S na Nọvemba 6, ebubo nke China gọnarịrị.

rows.source: Trump's accusation that Beijing was trying to meddle in U.S. elections marked what U.S. officials told Reuters was a new phase in an escalating campaign by Washington to put pressure on China.
rows.output: Nkwupụta Trump na Beijing na-agbalị ime ihe n'ụzọ na-adịghị mma na ntuli aka U.S. bụ ihe ngosi nke oge ọhụrụ na mgbasa ozi na-arị elu nke Washington na-agbalị ịmanye China.
rows.reference: Ebubo Trump na Beijing na-agbalị itinye aka na ntuli aka U.S gosiri ihe ndị ọrụ U.S gwara ndị Reuters na ọ bụ agba nke ọhụrụ na mgbakiri ala Washington na-abawanye ịkwagide China.

rows.source: While it is normal for foreign governments to place advertisements to promote trade, Beijing and Washington are currently locked in an escalating trade war that has seen them level rounds of tariffs on each other's imports.
rows.output: N'oge a na-adịkarị ka gọọmentị mba ọzọ na-etinye mgbasa ozi iji kwalite azụmahịa, Beijing na Washington na-alụ ọgụ azụmahịa na-aga n'ihu nke na-ahụ ha na-etinye usoro ụtụ isi na mbubata nke ibe ha.
rows.reference: Ebe ọ bụ ihe nkiti gọọmentị mba ofesi itinye mgbasa ozi iji kwalite ahịa, Beijing na Washington nọ na ndọrọndọrọ azụmahịa na-abawanye nke megoro ka ha tinye ụtụ ngwahịa na ahịa mbubadata ha.

rows.source: China's retaliatory tariffs early in the trade war were designed to hit exporters in states such as Iowa that supported Trump's Republican Party, Chinese and U.S. experts have said.
rows.output: Mmetụta ndị China na mbuso agha ahịa ahụ na mbido bụ iji kụọ ndị na-ebupụ ahịa na steeti dị ka Iowa nke kwadoro pati Republican nke Trump, ndị ọkà mmụta China na ndị America kwuru.
rows.reference: Ntinye ụtụ ngwahịa nke China mere na mbido agha azụmahịa ka emebere ka ọ metụta ndị na ebupu ahịa n’obodo dịka Iowa kwadoro otu ndọrọndọrọ Repọblikan nke Trump, ndị ọkammara China na U.S kwuru.

rows.source: Terry Branstad, the U.S. ambassador to China and the former longtime governor of Iowa, a major exporter of agricultural goods to China, said Beijing had hurt American workers, farmers and businesses.
rows.output: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchi anya US na China na onye bụbu gọvanọ Iowa, bụ onye na-ebupụta ihe ubi na China, kwuru na Beijing emeela ihe na-emerụ ndị ọrụ America, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa.
rows.reference: Terry Branstad, onye nnọchite anya U.S na China bụkwa onye chịburu Iowa, onye mbupu ahịa nri ubi nke ukwuu na China, kwuru na China merụrụ ndị ọrụ, ndị ọrụ ugbo na azụmahịa nke America ahụ.

rows.source: China, Branstad wrote in an opinion piece in Sunday's Des Moines Register, "is now doubling down on that bullying by running propaganda ads in our own free press."
rows.output: China, Branstad dere n'ime otu akụkọ dị na Sunday's Des Moines Register, "na-eme ka nrụgide ahụ dịkwuo elu site n'ịgba mgbasa ozi mgbasa ozi na mgbasa ozi anyị n'efu."
rows.reference: China, Branstad dere n’echiche ya na Des Moines Register na Sọnde, “na-ekwusi ike maka mmegide ahụ site na itinye mgbasa ozi n’akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi anyị.”

rows.source: "In disseminating its propaganda, China's government is availing itself of America's cherished tradition of free speech and a free press by placing a paid advertisement in the Des Moines Register," Branstad wrote.
rows.output: "N'ịgbasa mgbasa ozi ya, gọọmentị China na-eji omenala America nke nnwere onwe ikwusa na mgbasa ozi site n'inye akwụkwọ mgbapụta na Des Moines Register," Branstad dere.
rows.reference: “N’ịgbasa ozi asị a, gọọmentị China na ewere oghere omenala America hụrụ n’anya bụ nke onye kwuo uche ya na mgbasa ozi enweghị mkpagbu were tinye mgbasa ozi akwụrụ ụgwọ na Des Moines Register.” Branstad dere.

rows.source: "In contrast, at the newsstand down the street here in Beijing, you will find limited dissenting voices and will not see any true reflection of the disparate opinions that the Chinese people may have on China's troubling economic trajectory, given that media is under the firm thumb of the Chinese Communist Party," he wrote.
rows.output: "N'ụzọ dị iche, n'ụlọ ahịa akụkọ dị n'okporo ụzọ a na Beijing, ị ga-ahụ olu ndị na-emegide ya na-erughị ala ma ọ dịghịkwa ihe ngosi nke echiche dị iche iche ndị China nwere banyere ụzọ akụ na ụba China na-echegbu, n'ihi na mgbasa ozi dị n'okpuru mkpalị nke Chinese Communist Party."
rows.reference: “Ma ịtụlee ya n’ọdụ akwụkwọ mgbasa ozi dị n’okporo beijing ebe a, ịga ahụ na enwere obere olu ndịiche nke na ịghaghị ahụ ihe n’egosi n’ezie echiche di iche ndị China nwere ike nwee maka usoro akụnụba China nọ na nsogbu, ebe ọ bụ n’ụlọ mgbasa ozi nọ na njikwa nke China Communist Party,” ọ dere.

rows.source: He added that "one of China's most prominent newspapers dodged the offer to publish" his article, although he did not say which newspaper.
rows.output: Ọ gbakwunyere na "otu n'ime akwụkwọ akụkọ China kacha mara amara jụrụ inye ohere ka ebipụta" akwụkwọ ya, ọ bụ ezie na o kwuru na akwụkwọ akụkọ ahụ.
rows.reference: Ọ gbakwunyere na “otu n’ime akwụkwọ akụkọ ama ama na China zenarịrị ibiputa” ederede ya, n’agbanyeghị na o kwughị akwụkwọ akụkọ nke ọ bụ.

rows.source: Republicans Alienating Women Voters Ahead of Midterms With Kavanaugh Debacle, Analysts Warn
rows.output: Ndị Republican na-eme ka ndị na-eme ntuli aka na-ahụ maka ụmụ nwanyị na-eme ntuli aka na midterm na ihe mberede Kavanaugh, ndị na-ahụ maka ya na-adọ aka ná ntị.
rows.reference: Ndị Repọblikan Na-akpachapụ Ndị Ntuli Aka Ụmụ-nwanyị Tupu Ntuli Aka Ọkara Ọchịchị Maka Ọgbaghara Kavanaugh, Ndị Nyocha Dọrọ Aka na Ntị

rows.source: As many top Republicans stand-by and defend Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh in the face of several allegations of sexual assault, analyst have warned they will see a backlash, particularly from women, during the upcoming midterm elections.
rows.output: Ka ọ̀tụ̀tụ̀ ndị Republican kacha elu guzoro na-echebe onye a họpụtara maka Ụlọikpe Kasị Elu, Brett Kavanaugh, n'ihu ọtụtụ ebubo nke mwakpo mmekọahụ, ndị nyocha dọọ aka ná ntị na ha ga-ahụ azịza, ọkachasị site n'aka ụmụ nwanyị, n'oge ntuli aka nke etiti.
rows.reference: Dị ka ọtụtụ ndị isi Repọblikan kwụnyere ma kwuchitere Onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu Brett Kavanaugh n’ihu ebubo dị iche iche nke mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị, ndị nyocha adọọla aka na ntị na ha ga-ahụ ndapụta iwe ga-esite ọkachasị n’aka ụmụ-nwanyị, n’oge ntuli aka ọkara ọchịchị na-abịa.

rows.source: The emotions surrounding this have been extremely high, and most Republicans are on record already showing they wanted to go forward with a vote.
rows.output: Mmetụta dị n'ihe a na-eme ka ọ dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Republican edekọla na ha chọrọ ka ha gaa n'ihu na votu.
rows.reference: Mmetụta sochiri nke a dị elu nke ukwuu, na ọtụtụ ndị Repọblikan ka edekọbara na ha egosila na ha chọrọ ịga n’ihu mee ntuli aka.

rows.source: Those things can't be walked back," Grant Reeher, a professor of political science at Syracuse University's Maxwell School told The Hill for an article published Saturday.
rows.output: Ihe ndị ahụ enweghị ike ịlaghachi azụ," Grant Reeher, onye prọfesọ sayensị ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị na Mahadum Syracuse's Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka isiokwu nke e bipụtara na Satọde.
rows.reference: Enweghị ike iweghachi ihe ndị ahụ,” Grant Reeher, onye ọkammụta nke sayensị ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị na Syracuse University Maxwell School gwara The Hill maka ederede nke ebiputara na Satọde.

rows.source: Reeher said he doubts Senator Jeff Flake's (R-Arizona) last-minute push for an FBI investigation will be enough to placate angry voters.
rows.output: Reeher kwuru na o nweghị obi ike na onye omebe iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) na-awụpụta nyocha FBI n'oge ikpeazụ ga-ezu oke iji mee ka ndị na-ewute ha dị jụụ.
rows.reference: Reeher kwuru na ya na-agbagha n’ọkwụkwa ikpeazụ nke Onye Ọmebe Iwu Jeff Flake (R-Arizona) mere maka nyocha FBI a ga-ezu iji wetuo iwe ndị ntuli aka.

rows.source: "Women are not going to forget what happened yesterday - they are not going to forget it tomorrow and not in November," Karine Jean-Pierre, a senior adviser and national spokeswoman for the progressive group MoveOn said on Friday, according to the Washington, D.C. newspaper.
rows.output: "Ụmụnwaanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụbọchị gara aga - ha agaghị echefu ya echi, ha agaghị echefu ya n'ụbọchị iri na abụọ n'ọnwa Nọvemba," Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ pụrụ iche na onye na-ekwu okwu mba maka otu ndị na-eme mgbanwe MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dị ka akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C. si kwuo.
rows.reference: “Ụmụ-nwanyị agaghị echefu ihe mere ụnyahụ - ha agaghị echefu echi niile ma Nọvemba, “ Karine Jean-Pierre, onye ndụmọdụ senịọ na onye nkwuchite okwu obodo maka otu ọganihu MoveOn kwuru na Fraịde, dabere na akwụkwọ akụkọ Washington, D.C.

rows.source: On Friday morning, protestors chanted "November is coming!" as they demonstrated in the hallway of the Senate as the Republicans controlling the Judiciary Committee chose to move forward with Kavanaugh's nomination despite the testimony of Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic reported.
rows.output: N'ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị na-eme ngagharị iwe na-eti "November na-abịa!" ka ha na-eme ngagharị n'ụlọomeiwu nke Sineti ka ndị Republican na-achịkwa kọmitii ikpe na-eme mkpebi ịga n'ihu na nhọpụta Kavanaugh n'agbanyeghị okwu Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kọriri.
rows.reference: N’ụtụtụ Fraịde, ndị ngagharị iwe kwere ukwe “Nọvemba na-abịa!” ka ha na-agagharị ngagharị iwe n’ogologo ụzọ Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu ebe ndị Repọblikan ji Ọgbakọ Ọka Ikpe họrọ ịga n’ihu na nhọrọ Kavanaugh agbanyeghị nkwuputa Dr. Christine Blasey Ford, Mic kwuputara.

rows.source: "Democratic enthusiasm and motivation is going to be off the chart," Stu Rothenberg, a nonpartisan political analyst, told the news site.
rows.output: "Ọchịchọ ndị Democrats na mkpalite obi ike ga-adị elu," Stu Rothenberg, onye na-ahụ maka ndọrọ ndọrọ ọchịchị na-abụghị nke otu, gwara webụsaịtị akụkọ.
rows.reference: “Ịnụ ọkụ n’obi na mkpalite mmụọ nke Demokrat ga-apụ iche,” Stu Rothenberg, onye nyocha ndọrọndọrọ ọchịchị enweghị otu o binyere gwara ndị akụkọ.

rows.source: "People are saying it's already been high; that's true.
rows.output: Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke ahụ bụ eziokwu.
rows.reference: “Ndị mmadụ na-ekwu na ọ dịla elu; nke a bụ eziokwu.

rows.source: But it could be higher, particularly among swing women voters in the suburbs and younger voters, 18- to 29-year-olds, who while they don't like the president, often don't vote."
rows.output: Mana ọ nwere ike ịdị elu, ọkachasị n'etiti ndị na-eme ntụli aka nwanyị n'ime ime obodo na ndị na-eme ntụli aka na-eto eto, ndị dị afọ 18 ruo 29, bụ ndị ọ bụ ezie na ha anaghị amasị onye isi ala, na-emekarịghị ntụli aka."
rows.reference: Mana ọ nwere ike ịgbagokwu ọkachasị n’etiti ụmụ-nwanyị n’enweghị otu ha binyere n’ime obodo yana ndị ntuli aka na-etolite etolite, gbara afọ 18- ruo 29-, bụ ndị ebe onye isi ala anaghị amasị, anaghị eme ntuli aka kwa mgbe.”

rows.source: Even before Ford's public testimony detailing her allegations of sexual assault against the Supreme Court nominee, analysts suggested a backlash could follow if Republicans pushed forward with the confirmation.
rows.output: Ọbụna tupu Ford pụta n'ihu ọha ka o kwuo ebubo mmeso nwoke na nwanyị megide onye a họpụtara n'ụlọikpe Kasị Elu, ndị nyocha kwuru na a ga-enwe azịza ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Republican na-aga n'ihu na-akwado nkwado.
rows.reference: Ọbụlagodi tupu nkwuputanke ọha Ford mere na-akọwa ebubo mmekọrịta nwoke na nwanyị megide onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe kachasị Elu, ndị nyocha na-atụ elo na ndapụta iwe nwere ike sote ma ọ bụrụ na ndị Repọblikan gaa n’ihu mee nkwado ahụ.

rows.source: "This has become a muddled mess for the GOP," said Michael Steele, former chairman of the Republican National Committee, early last week, according to NBC News.
rows.output: "Nke a agbanwewo n'ime ihe na-adịghị mma maka ndị Republican," ka Michael Steele, onye bụbu onye isi oche nke Republican National Committee, kwuru n'isi izu gara aga, dị ka NBC News si kwuo.
rows.reference: “Nke a abụrụla ọgbaghara dịịrị GOP,” Michael Steele kwuru, onye isi chịburu Ọgbakọ Otu Repọblikan, na mbido izug ara aga, dabere na NBC News.

rows.source: "It's just not about the committee vote or the final vote or whether Kavanaugh is put on the bench, it's also about the way Republicans have handled this and how they have treated her," Guy Cecil, director of Priorities USA, a group that helps to elect Democrats, pointed out to the news channel.
rows.output: "Ọ bụghị naanị maka votu kọmitii ma ọ bụ votu ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma e tinyere Kavanaugh n'oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Republican si eme ihe na otu ha si eme ya," Guy Cecil, onye isi oche nke Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka na ntuli aka nke ndị Democrats, kwuru na netwọkọ akụkọ.
rows.reference: “Ọ bụghị naanị maka ntuli aka ndị ọgbakọ ma ọ bụ maka ntuli aka ikpeazụ ma ọ bụ ma etinyere Kavanaugh n’oche, ọ bụkwa maka otu ndị Repọblikan siri jikwaa ihe a ma ka ha siri meso ya omume,” Guy Cecil, onye isi Priorities USA, otu na-enyere aka ahọpụta ndị Demokrat, rụtụrụ ndị akụkọ aka.

rows.source: However, Americans appear to be somewhat split over who to believe in the wake of Ford's and Kavanaugh's testimonies, with slightly more siding with the latter.
rows.output: Ọbụna, ndị America yiri ka ha na-ekewa echiche banyere onye ha ga-ekwere mgbe Ford na Kavanaugh mechara kwuo okwu, na obere ndị na-akwado Ford.
rows.reference: Kaosiladị, Ndị America dị ka ndị kewara ekewa n’onye ha ga-ekwenyere na ndapụta nkwuputa Ford na Kavanaugh, ebe ndị karịrị kwụnyere onye nke ikpeazụ.

rows.source: A new poll from YouGov shows that 41 percent of respondents definitely or probably believed Ford's testimony, while 35 percent said they definitely or probably believed Kavanaugh.
rows.output: Nleba anya ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov na-egosi na 41 pasent nke ndị zaghachirinụ kwenyere na nkwupụta Ford, ebe 35 pasent kwuru na ha kwenyere na nkwupụta Kavanaugh.
rows.reference: Nyocha ọhụrụ sitere na YouGov gosiri na pesentị 41 ndị zara ajụjụ kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ nkwuputa Ford, ebe pesentị 35 kwuru na ha kwenyere kpamkpam ma ọ bụ kwenyetụrụ Kavanaugh.

rows.source: Additionally, 38 percent said they thought Kavanaugh has probably or definitely lied during his testimony, while just 30 percent said the same about Ford.
rows.output: N'otu aka ahụ, 38 pasentị ndị mmadụ kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh nwere ike ma ọ bụ na ọ ga-aghọgbu n'oge nnọkọ ya, ebe naanị 30 pasentị kwuru otu ihe ahụ gbasara Ford.
rows.reference: Na mgbakwunye, pesentị 38 kwuru na ha chere na Kavanaugh eleghị anya sịrị asị ma ọ bụ sịa asị kpamkpam n’oge nkwuputa ya, ebe naanị pesentị 30 kwuru otu ihe ahụ maka Ford.

rows.source: After the push from Flake, the FBI is currently investigating the allegations brought forward by Ford as well as at least one other accuser, Deborah Ramirez, The Guardian reported.
rows.output: Mgbe ọkpọkpu si na Flake, ndị FBI na-enyocha ebubo ndị Ford na opekempe onye na-ekwu okwu ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez, dị ka Guardian si kwuo.
rows.reference: Ka Flake mechara nkwanye, ndị FBI na-eme nyocha ugbu a n’ebubo Ford boro, yana opekempe otu onye ebubo ọzọ, Deborah Ramirez mere, The Guardian kwuputara.

rows.source: Ford testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee under oath last week that Kavanaugh drunkenly assaulted her at the age of 17.
rows.output: N'oge na-adịbeghị anya, Ford gbara aka n'ihu kọmitii ikpe ziri ezi nke Senate n'okpuru iyi na Kavanaugh wakporo ya mgbe ọ dị afọ iri na asaa.
rows.reference: Ford mere nkwuputa n’ihu Ọgbakọ Ndị Ikpe Nzụkọ Ọmeiwu n’okpuru iyi n’izu gara aga na Kavanaugh dakporo ya n’anya mmanya mgbe ọ gbara afọ 17.

rows.source: Ramirez alleges that the Supreme Court nominee exposed his genitals to her while they attended a party during their time studying at Yale in the 1980s.
rows.output: Ramirez na-ekwu na onye a họpụtara n'ụlọikpe Kasị Elu kpughere ihe dị n'ahụ́ ya nye ya mgbe ha nọ na nnọkọ n'oge ha na-amụ ihe na Yale n'afọ 1980.
rows.reference: Ramirez boro ebubo n’onye nhọpụta Ụlọ Ikpe Kachasị Elu ahụ gosiri ya ike ya mgbe ha na-eme ọgbakọ oriri na ọṅụṅụ n’oge ha na-agụ akwụkwọ na Yale n’ime 1980s.

rows.output: Onye chepụtara Intanet Wide World na-eme atụmatụ ịmalite Intanet ọhụrụ iji were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were were
rows.reference: Onye Mmepụta World Wide Web Na-ama Atụmatụ Ịmalite Ịntanetị Ọhụrụ Iji Sonyere Google na Facebook

rows.source: Tim Berners-Lee, the inventor of the World Wide Web, is launching a startup that seeks to rival Facebook, Amazon and Google.
rows.output: Tim Berners-Lee, onye chepụtara World Wide Web, na-ebupụta ụlọ ọrụ na-achọ ịlụso Facebook, Amazon na Google ọgụ.
rows.reference: Tim Berners-Lee, onye mmepụta World Wide Web, na-amalite ụlọ ọrụ ọhụrụ nke ga-achụso Facebook, Amazon na Google.

rows.source: The technology legend's latest project, Inrupt, is a company that builds off of Berners-Lee's open source platform Solid.
rows.output: Onye na-eme ihe nkiri teknụzụ ọhụrụ nke onye na-eme ihe nkiri na-eme ihe nkiri, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-ewu ihe na ntọala Solid nke Berners-Lee mepere emepe.
rows.reference: Atụmatụ ọhụrụ ahụ nke ọkaibe teknụzụ, Inrupt, bụ ụlọ ọrụ na-agbakwasa ụkwụ na ngwanro ghe oghe Berners-Lee, Solid.

rows.source: Solid allows users to choose where their data is stored and what people are allowed to have access to what information.
rows.output: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere iji họrụ ebe data ha ga-echekwa na onye nwere ike ịnweta ozi ụfọdụ.
rows.reference: Solid na-enye ndị ọrụ oghere ịhọrọ ebe ha ga-echekwa data ha yana ozi ndị mmadụ nwere ike nweta.

rows.source: In an exclusive interview with Fast Company, Berners-Lee joked that the intent behind Inrupt is "world domination."
rows.output: N'ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche na Fast Company, Berners-Lee na-akwa emo na ebumnuche dị n'azụ Inrupt bụ "ịchịkwa ụwa."
rows.reference: N’ajụjụ ọnụ pụrụ iche Fast Company mere, Berners-Lee mara njakịrị na ebumnuche ejiri mebe Inrupt bụ “ịchị mba ụwa.”

rows.source: "We have to do it now," he said of the startup.
rows.output: "Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a," ka o kwuru banyere ụlọ ọrụ ahụ.
rows.reference: “Anyị ga-eme ya ugbu a,” o kwuru maka ụlọ ọhụrụ ahụ.

rows.source: "It's a historical moment."
rows.output: "Ọ bụ oge akụkọ ihe mere eme."
rows.reference: “Ọ bụ oge a ga-edebanye na akụkọ.”

rows.source: The app uses Solid's technology to allow people to create their own "personal online data store" or a POD.
rows.output: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid mee ka ndị mmadụ nwee ike ịmepụta ebe nchekwa data nke ha n'onwe ha ma ọ bụ POD.
rows.reference: Ngwa ahụ na-eji teknụzụ Solid enye ndị mmadụ oghere imepụta “ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị” ma ọ bụ POD.

rows.source: It can contain contact lists, to-do lists, calendar, music library and other personal and professional tools.
rows.output: O nwere ike ịnwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe ga-eme, kalenda, ụlọ akwụkwọ egwu na ngwa ndị ọzọ nke onwe na nke ọrụ.
rows.reference: Ọ nwere ike inwe ndepụta kọntaktị, ndepụta ihe omume, kalenda, ọba egwu yana ngwa nkeonwe na nke eji arụ ọrụ.

rows.source: It's like Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack and Spotify are all available on one browser and all at the same time.
rows.output: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n'otu ihe nchọgharị ma dịkwa n'otu oge.
rows.reference: Ọ dị ka Google Drive, Microsoft Outlook, Slack na Spotify dị n’otu nchọgharị ma ha niile n’otu oge.

rows.source: What's unique about the personal online data store is that it is completely up to the user who can access what kind of information.
rows.output: Ihe pụrụ iche gbasara ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n'ịntanetị bụ na ọ dị n'ikike onye ọrụ ịnweta ụdị ozi dị iche iche.
rows.reference: Ihe pụrụ iche na ebe nchekwa data nkeonwe n’ịntanetị bụ na ọ dịịrị naanị onye ji ya arụ ọrụ ịhọrọ onye ga-enweta ozi nke ọ bụla.

rows.source: The company calls it "personal empowerment through data."
rows.output: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya "ike nke onwe site na data."
rows.reference: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ na-akpọ ya “ikike nkeonwe site na data.”

rows.source: The idea for Inrupt, according to the company's CEO John Bruce, is for the company to bring resources, process and appropriate skills to help make Solid available to everyone.
rows.output: Echiche maka Inrupt, dị ka CEO nke ụlọ ọrụ ahụ bụ John Bruce si kwuo, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ ahụ wee wetara ihe onwunwe, usoro na nkà dị mkpa iji nyere aka mee ka Solid dịruru onye ọ bụla.
rows.reference: Ebumnuche Inrupt, dabere na CEO John Bruce, bụ ka ụlọ ọrụ kpokọba, akụrụngwa, usoro na nka dabara daba iji nyere aka mee ka Solid rute onye ọ bụla.

rows.source: The company currently consists of Berners-Lee, Bruce, a security platform bought by IBM, some on-staff developers contracted to work on the project, and a community of volunteer coders.
rows.output: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ ugbu a nwere Berners-Lee, Bruce, ikpo okwu nchekwa nke IBM zụrụ, ụfọdụ ndị mmepe nọ n'ọrụ na-arụ ọrụ na ọrụ ahụ, na obodo nke ndị na-eme koodu na-enye onwe ha.
rows.reference: Ụlọ ọrụ ahụ nwere naanị Berners-Lee, Bruce, ebe nchekwa IBM zụtara na ya, ndị ọrụ nrụpụta ewere n’ọrụ ịrụ n’atụmatụ ahụ yana ọgbakọ ndị koodu wepụtara onwe ha.

rows.source: Starting this week, technology developers around the world could create their own decentralized apps using the tools available on the Inrupt website.
rows.output: N'izu a, ndị mmepe teknụzụ n'ụwa niile nwere ike ịmepụta ngwa ha nke ha na-enweghị isi site na ngwa ndị dị na webụsaịtị Inrupt.
rows.reference: Site n’izu a, ndị nrụpụta teknụzụ ụwa gbaa gburugburu ga-enwe ike mebe ngwa agaghị ekpokọba ọnụ nke ha site n’iji ngwa mebere na websaịtị Inrupt.

rows.source: Berners-Lee said that he and his team are not talking to "Facebook and Google about whether or not to introduce a complete change where all their business models are completely upended overnight.
rows.output: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya na ndị otu ya anaghị ekwu okwu na "Facebook na Google banyere ma ọ bụ na ha ga-ebelata mgbanwe zuru oke ebe usoro azụmahịa ha niile na-agbanwe n'otu abalị.
rows.reference: Berners-Lee kwuru na ya ndị otu ya anaghị agwa ndị “Facebook na Google okwu banyere ma ha a ga-amalite ma ọ bụ hapụ mmalite mgbanwe kpamkpam ebe ụdịdị azụmahịa na-atụgharị ozugbo na ntabi anya.

rows.source: "We are not asking their permission."
rows.output: "Anyị anaghị arịọ ha ka ha nye anyị ikike."
rows.reference: “Anyị anaghị anata ha ikike.”

rows.source: In a post on Medium published on Saturday, Berners-Lee wrote that Inrupt's "mission is to provide commercial energy and an ecosystem to help protect the integrity and quality of the new web built on Solid."
rows.output: N'akwụkwọ ozi e bipụtara na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na ebumnobi Inrupt bụ "inye ike azụmahịa na ecosystem iji nyere aka chebe ịdị n'otu na ịdị mma nke webụ ọhụrụ a na-ewu na Solid."
rows.reference: Na mbipụta emere na Medium na Satọde, Berners-Lee dere na “ebumnuche Inrupt bụ inye ike azụmahịa na gburugburu inyere aka chekwaa ntụkwasị obi na ịdị mma weebu ọhụrụ ahụ arụrụ na Solid.”

rows.source: In 1994, Berners-Lee transformed the Internet when he established the World Wide Web Consortium at Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.output: N'afọ 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ hiwere World Wide Web Consortium na Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
rows.reference: Na 1994, Berners-Lee gbanwere Ịntanetị mgbe ọ mepụtara World Wide Web Consortuim na Massachusetts Institue of Technology.

rows.source: In recent months, Berners-Lee has been an influential voice in the net neutrality debate.
rows.output: N'ọnwa ndị na-adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee enweela olu na-ekwu okwu na arụmụka nke neutrality n'ịntanetị.
rows.reference: N’ọnwa ndị adịbeghị anya, Berners-Lee bụ olu na-ada ụda na arụmarụ ụka nnwere onwe ọrụ ịntanetị.

rows.source: Even while launching Inrupt, Berners-Lee will remain the Founder and Director of World Wide Web Consortium, the Web Foundation and the Open Data Institute.
rows.output: Ọbụna mgbe ha na-ebupụta Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọgide na onye guzobere na onye isi ụlọ ọrụ World Wide Web Consortium, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.
rows.reference: Ọbulagodi mgbe a na-ebuputa Inrupt, Berners-Lee ga-anọrọ dịka onye Mmepụta na Onye Isi nke World Wide Web Consortuim, Web Foundation na Open Data Institute.

rows.source: "I'm incredibly optimistic for this next era of the web," Berners-Lee added.
rows.output: "Ana m enwe obi ụtọ nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa nke ịntanetị."
rows.reference: “A na m enwe olile anya nke ukwuu maka oge na-abịa n’ihu nke weebu,” Berners-Lee gbakwunyere.

rows.source: Bernard Vann: WW1 Victoria Cross cleric celebrated
rows.output: Bernard Vann: Onye na-eme ihe nkiri Victoria Cross nke WW1 na-eme ememe
rows.reference: Bernard Vann: Emere emume onye ụkọchukwu Victoria Cross WW1

rows.source: The only Church of England cleric to win a Victoria Cross during World War One as a combatant has been celebrated in his hometown 100 years on.
rows.output: Onye ụkọchukwu Anglican naanị nke meriri Victoria Cross n'oge Agha Ụwa Mbụ dị ka onye agha ka a na-eme ememe n'obodo ya afọ 100 ka e mesịrị.
rows.reference: Emeela emume nke naanị ụkọchukwu Church of England nwetara mmeri Victoria Cross n’oge World War One dị ka onye agha n’obodo ya ka afọ gbara 100.

rows.source: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann won the award on 29 September 1918 in the attack at Bellenglise and Lehaucourt.
rows.output: Lt Col The Reverend Bernard Vann meriri ihe nrite ahụ na 29 Septemba 1918 n'oge mwakpo ahụ na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.
rows.reference: Lt Col Ụkọchukwu Bernard Vann nwetara awọdụ na 29, Septemba 1918 na mbuso agha emere na Bellenglise na Lehaucourt.

rows.source: However, he was killed by a sniper four days later and never knew he had won the highest British military honour.
rows.output: Ọbụna, e gburu ya site n'aka onye na-agba égbè ụbọchị anọ ka e mesịrị, ọ maghịkwa na ọ meriri ihe nrite agha kacha elu nke ndị Bekee.
rows.reference: Kaosiladị, mgbọ ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe tụrụ ya ka ụbọchị anọ gachara na ọ maghị ncha ncha na etubere ya ugo ndị agha kachasị na Britain.

rows.source: A commemorative stone was unveiled by his two grandsons at a parade in Rushden, Northamptonshire, on Saturday.
rows.output: A na-ekpughe okwute ncheta site n'aka ụmụ nwoke abụọ ya n'oge mmemme na Rushden, Northamptonshire, na Satọde.
rows.reference: Ụmụ ụmụ ya ndị nwoke abụọ kpughere okwute iji na-eme ncheta ya na ngarube emere na Rushden, Northamptonshire, na Satọde.

rows.source: One of his grandsons, Michael Vann, said it was "brilliantly symbolic" the stone would be revealed exactly 100 years on from his grandfather's award-winning feat.
rows.output: Otu n'ime ụmụ-ọmụ ya, Michael Vann, kwuru na ọ bụ "ihe ngosi nke ọma" na a ga-ekpughe okwute ahụ kpọmkwem afọ 100 ka e mesịrị ihe ndị nna nna ya rụzuru.
rows.reference: Otu n’ime nwa nwa ya Michael Vann, kwuru na ọ bụ “ihe nrịbama pụrụ iche nke ukwuu” na a ga-ekpughe okwute ahụ ka afọ gbara 100 kpọmkwem site na mgbe nna ya ochie kpara ike o jiri nweta awọdụ.

rows.source: According to the London Gazette, on 29 September 1918 Lt Col Vann led his battalion across the Canal de Saint-Quentin "through a very thick fog and under heavy fire from field and machine guns."
rows.output: N'afọ 1918, 29 Septemba, Lt Col Vann duru ndị agha ya gafee Canal de Saint-Quentin "site na nnukwu ọkụ na-afụ na mgbọrọgwụ na mgbọrọgwụ."
rows.reference: Dabere na London Gazette, na 29 Septemba 1918 Lt Col Vann kpọọrọ ndị otu agha ya gafee Canal de Saint-Quentin “n’etiti urukpuru ojii yana n’ime nnukwu ọkụ ọgbụgba sitere na ama yana egbe.”

rows.source: He later rushed up to the firing line and with the "greatest gallantry" led the line forward before rushing a field-gun single-handed and knocked out three of the detachment.
rows.output: Ọ mechara bilie gaa n'ihu n'ahịrị na-edu ndị agha ahụ n'ihu tupu ọ bilie n'otu ụgbọ agha ma kwụsị atọ n'ime ndị otu ahụ.
rows.reference: Ọ mechara gbara ọsọ gbabanye na ndị na-akwa mgbọ ma “kpaa ike ọkpara” duru ahịrị na-aga ihu tupu ọ chụrụ egbe naanị ya were kụpụ mmadụ ndị agha atọ nọpụrụ iche.

rows.source: Lt Col Vann was killed by a German sniper on 4 October 1918 - just over a month before the war ended.
rows.output: Ọkachamara Lt Col Vann gburu onye na-agba égbè German na 4 Ọktoba 1918 - ihe na-erughị ọnwa na agha ahụ gwụchara.
rows.reference: Onye ọkaibe n’ịgba egbe nke Germany gburu Lt Col Vann na 4 Oktoba 1918 - naanị otu ọnwa tupu agha akwụsị.
